end.summary:
Distinguished observation, hypothesis, law, and theory using dolphin and salt-water examples.
Correctly classified two sets of examples without help.
Explained that a hypothesis can be tested and may be rejected by evidence.
Repeated the misconception that theories turn into laws and laws are higher than theories; it was not corrected later.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Tara practised separating observations, hypotheses, laws, and theories using testable examples. They clearly described checking a hypothesis with a thermometer and recognising when evidence could show an idea was wrong. A mix-up remained: they said theories turn into laws and that laws are higher; this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask Tara to make a two-column note comparing the scientific meanings of “law” and “theory,” with one example of each.
